Assistant A answers both parts of the question and explains how superposition relates to entanglement: superposition allows the creation of entangled states, so entangled systems are in a joint superposition. It also mentions applications and the broader implications. It has minor flaws, such as a loose description of superposition as "multiple states simultaneously" and a redundant sentence about distance. It also says "entanglement can be used to create quantum computers," which is slightly imprecise. Still, it is accurate overall and addresses the relationship the user asked about.

Assistant B gives two brief, accurate definitions, including the linear-combination principle of superposition. However, it never explains how the two concepts relate, which was the core of the question. It is also very thin on depth.

Assistant A is more complete and more directly responsive.
